3. Silver finds a crumpled note in the trash can: **325003225300469**. The first try fails at the 5th digit, so the password has 5 digits.
4. Read **Archer's notebook**, lying next to a Persian statue in the big hall on the south side of the ruins. It has four pages (answer "Keep reading?" to turn them); pages 1, 2 and 4 end with the hints *"Three digits"*, *"Index number"* and *"What it stands on"*. Split the number into three-digit Pokédex numbers: 325 Spoink, 003 Venusaur, 225 Delibird, 300 Skitty, 469 Yanmega. Count the legs each one stands on.
5. Talk to Green/Red → **"Let me guess"** and enter **1 4 2 4 6**. A wrong digit gives "Beep! Error!"; you can retry as often as you like.
6. The passage opens with a noise in the room to the south. Go there: the Persian statue next to Archer's notebook has slid aside and uncovered a staircase (Silver comments as you walk up to it). Go down, and at the next Persian statue Silver's face opens it. The statue closes behind you, so the only way out is through the Rocket base (exit via the Mahogany Town shop).

quests.title: Mahogany Town → Team Rocket HQ: the radio-wave investigation (story; where to go next)
evidence: **Who gets it / when:** straight after the Lake of Rage red Gyarados chapter ([Lake of Rage: the red Gyarados and the radio transmitters](12-lake-of-rage-to-sinjoh.md#lake-of-rage-the-red-gyarados-and-the-radio-transmitters-story-how-to-move-on)). Walk up to the souvenir shop door and Gold, Crystal, Lance and Pryce go in with you.

**How it works:**
1. **The shop search.** The clerk denies everything and nothing turns up. Talk to **Pryce** in the shop: he tells you to search *outside*, around the shop, for other places Team Rocket could hide. The answer is the Team Rocket base in Mt. Mortar and its hidden passage (the Boot Camp Ruins at the east end of Mt. Mortar B1F; see [the previous entry](#boot-camp-ruins-the-team-rocket-pc-password-story-mahogany-rocket-base-chapter) for the password). You enter B1F from that passage, with Green (Red for female players) and Silver.
2. **B1F.** As you arrive, a Grunt battles you (Spiritomb 62, Charizard 63, Octillery 64, Roselia 65; losing whites you out). The Persian statues are cameras. Walking in front of one (three spots) calls two Grunts into a Double Battle. Some floor tiles are traps that start wild battles with a Koffing (Lv. 21), Voltorb (Lv. 23) or Geodude (Lv. 21). In the control room at the south end of the floor, Green/Red and Silver make the operator unlock every passage. The shop's hidden stairs open too, and Lance, Pryce, Gold and Crystal join you. There's a **Sun Stone** item ball on this floor.
3. **B2F.**
   - Butch and Cassidy block the east side with a 2-on-1 Double Battle.
   - **Scientist Fujimoto** stands in a corner on the east side, about halfway down the floor ("What are you doing in this corner?!"). Beat him and pick up the **Secret Key** item ball beside him (you need it on B3F).
   - Silver is losing to Karen. "Help Silver?" **Yes** starts a battle with Karen (Lv. 90). No does nothing, and you can come back to it. Karen isn't missable: Silver leaves once Archer's room is done, but Karen stays on B2F until you beat her, and talking to her still starts the battle (tested in an emulator after the chapter).
   - The sealed door in the middle wants the spoken password "Team Rocket will rule the world!" in Petrel's voice. Saying it yourself always fails ("Voiceprint mismatch").
4. **B3F** (full walkthrough: [Team Rocket HQ B3F: the two passwords and the Secret Key door](12-lake-of-rage-to-sinjoh.md#team-rocket-hq-b3f-the-two-passwords-and-the-secret-key-door-continues-battle-frontier-cianwood-city-and-mahogany-towns-mahogany-town--team-rocket-hq)).
   - Charon and Cyrus take you on in a **Double Battle**. Afterwards Gold tells you the first password: **"Slowpoke Tail"**.
   - Ariana and Lawrence challenge you to a **Multi Battle**, with Crystal as your partner.
   - **Scientist Watanabe** guards a PC. Beat him and he gives you the second password: **"Raticate Tail"**.
   - The door to the Executives' room needs the **Secret Key** and both passwords. Behind it, "Giovanni" turns out to be **Petrel** in disguise; beat him. Then go on to Archer's room.
5. **Archer's room.** Proton and the Marauder take you on in a Double Battle, and **Archer attacks straight after with no healing in between**, so go in healed and carry restoring items. If you lose either battle you black out. Pryce saves Prof. Hale, and Petrel's **Chatot** is left behind repeating Petrel's line. Everyone goes back to the B2F door and the Chatot opens it.
6. **The radio room.** Electrode are wired into the machine in two rows. Yours is the one at the south end of the west row, the one that asks "Stop it?". Answer **Yes** and fight a wild **Electrode (Lv. 50)**. Beating it, catching it or running away all count. Your friends deal with the rest. Pryce's radio then works again, and the chapter ends.

**Notes:**
- **Don't miss the Rainbow Wing.** It's an item ball in Archer's room. Morty needs it in Ecruteak before you can climb the Bell Tower ([Bell Tower: Ho-Oh is stolen](10-ecruteak-olivine.md#bell-tower-ho-oh-is-stolen-league-hq-round-4-continues-pokémon-league-mt-silver-and-new-bark-towns-league-hq-entry)). The shop guard lets you back into the base afterwards ("you're the League Champion"), so you can fetch it later.
- Archer's notebook in the same room tells how Team Rocket used Prof. Hale. Reading it is optional.
- **Petrel's Chatot (one chance):** when the radio-room scene ends, everyone leaves except Petrel's Chatot, about six steps south and two east of where you're standing. Talk to it **before you leave B2F**: "Petrel's Chatot. Nobody wants it anymore. Catch it?" → **Yes** starts a wild battle with a **Chatot (Lv. 10)** you can catch. After that battle the Chatot is gone, however it ends (caught, knocked out, run from, or a loss that whites you out), and if you leave the floor without talking to it, it's gone for good. Tested in an emulator: the Chatot is still there after the scene and offers the battle.

quests.title: Whirl Islands: catch Lugia (after the final Hall of Fame)
evidence: **Who gets it / when:** Lugia is first stolen during the League HQ's round-4 story ([League HQ: the Trainer Affairs Department's investigations](07-league-to-cherrygrove.md#league-hq-the-trainer-affairs-departments-investigations-where-to-go-next)): Executive Lawrence uses the legendary birds to wake Lugia. You battle a Rocket pair, Lawrence and then Lugia itself, but he catches it anyway. That part is story. Lugia comes back for you **after your final Hall of Fame entry**.

**How it works:**
1. In the Ecruteak Dance Theater, tell Satsuki **"I want to see Lugia"** (see [Dance Theater → Bell Tower: catch Ho-Oh](10-ecruteak-olivine.md#dance-theater--bell-tower-catch-ho-oh-after-the-final-hall-of-fame)). The five Kimono Girls go to the Whirl Islands.
2. In Lugia's cave, talk to Satsuki and say **Yes** to starting the ritual. The Tidal Bell cutscene plays and Lugia appears.
3. Talk to Lugia → **Yes**: a normal wild battle with **Lugia, Lv. 95**. You can throw balls.

**Notes:**
- **Warning: one chance. Save first.** Catching it, knocking it out or running away all remove Lugia for good ([known issue](known-issues.md#lugia-one-chance)). Only a loss lets you retry: you white out and Lugia stays. You don't need to carry the Tidal Bell.
- **If you've already caught Ho-Oh but not Lugia,** Satsuki's first menu only offers "I want to see Lugia" and "Never mind". Choosing Lugia there wrongly takes the Ho-Oh path ("the Clear Bell is still in Morty's hands"). Talk to her again and choose Lugia from the full menu. *(Suspected hack bug; it also re-arms the Ho-Oh chain, see [the known issue](known-issues.md#satsukis-lugia-option).)*

quests.title: Frontier Access: the damaged stone and Jirachi (after the final Hall of Fame)
evidence: **Who gets it / when:** after your final Hall of Fame entry. Before that, examining the stone only shows "A hard stone. It has some obvious damage." The man explains that it was dug up while the Frontier was being built and nothing could break it.

**How it works:**
1. Examine the stone: "It looks like a Star Piece would fill in the broken part perfectly. Use a Star Piece to repair the stone?" → **Yes**. Each repair takes a Star Piece if you have one, but still counts if you have none ([known issue](known-issues.md#jirachi-stone-without-star-pieces)).
2. Keep choosing Yes. If you've finished the legendary investigation story (it ends in Cherrygrove City, when Crystal takes Suicune back to the orphanage), the stone wakes after **7 repairs** (tested in an emulator). **Warning:** if that story isn't finished, it needs more repairs, and waking Jirachi stops that story's remaining scenes from playing. Finish it first ([known issue](known-issues.md#jirachi-stone-and-the-story-counter)).
3. The stone turns into **Jirachi**. Two Team Rocket stragglers run in and try to make it grant their wish (a world ruled by Team Rocket). Nothing happens, and you fight them in a **Double Battle**: Grunts with Honchkrow 65, Weavile 64, Butterfree 63 and Gyarados 65, Rampardos 63, Gallade 64.
4. Win, and they give up Team Rocket. The man asks you to give Jirachi a safe home. Talk to Jirachi → "Take it with you on your journey?" → **Yes**.

**Notes:**
- If you lose the Double Battle you white out. The stone comes back, and the next repair wakes Jirachi and replays the scene.
- With a full party Jirachi won't join ("Your party is full"). Make room and talk to it again.

quests.title: Route 44: the kid with his brother's Heracross (→ Never-Melt Ice)
evidence: **Who gets it / when:** any time.

**How it works:**
1. Talk to either kid. The boy's Heracross flattens the Sneasel, then he asks if you want "a taste of Heracross's power". Answer **Yes**. If you say No he asks again, and you can say Yes then. You fight **Bug Catcher Nate** (a Lv. 82 Heracross plus three Lv. 7 cocoons). When he loses he blurts out that it's his big brother's Heracross, and he runs off to his brother.
2. Before this, the brother only says his little brother keeps borrowing his Pokémon. Now talk to the brother and accept his battle: **Ace Trainer Burke** (Politoed, Pinsir, Heracross, Scizor, Armaldo, Butterfree, Lv. 81–82). If you say No to him, he just ends the talk; talk to him again.
3. He recognises you as the Champion and asks what you thought of his brother. Both answers ("He used Heracross well" / "Never saw his Pokémon") lead to the same talk about growing up with your own Pokémon.
**Reward:** **Never-Melt Ice** (once).
**Notes:** losing either battle whites you out. You can retry.

quests.title: Ice Path 1F: the Icy Rock duel (→ Icy Rock)
evidence: **Who gets it / when:** any time.

**How it works:**
1. Walk up to either Trainer. They play out their "third duel today" and tie again. "Talk to them?" → **Battling over who gets an item?**
2. → **I want the Icy Rock too.** They agree on a new rule: beat both of them **back to back** and the rock is yours. "Want in?" → Yes.
3. Battle **Ace Trainer Sue** (Glalie, Piloswine, Aron Lv. 1, Lucario, Swampert; Lv. 81–82) and **Veteran Frost** (Abomasnow, Jynx, Castform, Walrein, Mamoswine; Lv. 81–82), one after the other with **no healing in between**. Which of them goes first depends on where you stand.
4. Win both and pick up the **Icy Rock** item ball.
**Reward:** **Icy Rock**. Afterwards Frost stands on the east side of the floor, about 14 steps north and 9 west of the exit to Blackthorn City, and offers a **repeatable rematch**, Single or Double Battle (Double needs two Pokémon).

**Notes:** these are Lv. 81–82 teams, far above the route's other Trainers. Losing either battle whites you out, but nothing is lost: talk to them again to retry. "None of my business" or "Never mind" just ends the talk.

2. Walk to the spot where he keeps them, right beside the Dragonite. A man with a Zangoose is trying to catch the hurt Pokémon to sell. Dragonite drives him off, then keeps rampaging.

quests.title: Reversal Cave: chase Giovanni through the Distortion World (story; warp-pad maze)

3. Where it drops you, step north. Giovanni gets ready to summon Giratina and leaves Charon to hold you off: **Executive Charon** (Muk 87, Drapion 88, Gengar 87, Dragalge 88, Rotom 87, Banette 88). If you lose, you white out and have to come back.

quests.title: Ice Path B2F: the cursed tunnel, Swinub and the Anti-Age Spray (needed in the final chapter)
evidence: **Who gets it / when:** any time after the Team Rocket HQ chapter. You **need** the spray in the final chapter: Giovanni and Cyrus go through this tunnel, and the kid turns you back at the entrance unless you carry an Anti-Age Spray.

**How it works:**
1. **Swinub Trainer.** His Swinub ran into the tunnel and came out old and frail. He's waiting for Durin Berries from Mahogany ([Mahogany Pokémon Center: Durin Berries for the Ice Path](11-cianwood-mahogany.md#mahogany-pokémon-center-durin-berries-for-the-ice-path--15-durin-berries)). Talk to him with **at least 10 Durin Berries**: he takes 10 and gives you a **Sacred Ash**. With fewer than 10 he turns you away.
2. **Old man (west).** Before step 1 he only warns you about the curse. After it, choose **"How do I get through?"**. He explains the spray and gives the recipe.
3. Bring him **10 Durin Berries, 5 Rare Candies, 1 Sacred Ash, 1 Fresh Water and $10,000**, then choose **"Make me an Anti-Age Spray"**. He takes it all and gives you the **Anti-Age Spray**. Missing anything: "You don't have enough ingredients" (or not enough money); nothing is taken.
4. **At the tunnel.** The kid stops you ("Hey! Wait up!"). If you carry the spray, you use it and may go in. Without it you're turned back.
**Reward:** access to the tunnel and the statue at its end (see below). The Swinub Trainer's Sacred Ash.

**Notes:**
- **You need 20 Durin Berries in total** (10 for Swinub, 10 for the spray). The Mahogany nurse gives 15 and Fuchsia City gives 1, so you'll have to grow more in Berry Pots or soft soil (not confirmed in game; see [the known issue](known-issues.md#durin-berries-for-the-anti-age-spray)). Sacred Ash also comes from item balls and a Vermilion trade, so you can use the Swinub one or another.
- The old man says each bottle covers one trip and that he'll make more. In fact the spray is **never used up**: keep it in the Bag and it works every time. He refuses to make a second while you hold one.
- Until you win the battle in Dialga's space (final chapter), the tunnel re-locks every time you re-enter the floor, so keep the spray. After that battle it stays open. Your final Hall of Fame entry locks it once more; one more use of the spray then opens it for good.
- The kid calls the tunnel cursed when he stops you. Only when you talk to him while it's already open does he say he "can't feel the curse anymore".
- **The final-chapter scene** (east section, a few steps north of the B3F stairs, after the Reversal Cave chapter): Giovanni has Giratina break the curse; the boy who had turned into an old man (a few steps east of the stairs) is young again, and Giovanni and Cyrus walk through the tunnel.
- **The statue at the end:** in the final chapter, after that scene, it "is giving off a mysterious power" and sends you to **Dialga's space**. After your final Hall of Fame it works only if you carry the **Adamant Orb** ("The statue is resonating with the Adamant Orb you carry!"). Any other time it's just "An ancient Pokémon statue."

quests.title: Dialga's and Palkia's spaces: Team Rocket catches Dialga and Palkia (story)
evidence: **Who gets it / when:** final chapter, straight after the Distortion World (previous entry).

**How it works:**
1. **Dialga's space.** Walk north from the statue, about 20 steps. Giovanni is forcing Dialga into a Special Ball and tells Cyrus to hold you off: **Executive Cyrus** (Crobat 89, Weavile 90, Gyarados 90, Honchkrow 90, Luxray 89, Gastrodon 89). After you win, Giovanni lets slip that the Lustrous Orb opens the way to Palkia "in the deepest part of Mt. Mortar". He escapes with the Adamant Orb, and Dialga is gone with him.
2. **Mt. Mortar.** Go to the ancient statue on B1F, beat Ariana there ([Mt. Mortar: the five-member expedition](11-cianwood-mahogany.md#mt-mortar-the-five-member-expedition-the-way-to-the-altar-needed-in-the-final-chapter), Notes) and the statue sends you to the south end of Palkia's space.
3. **Palkia's space.** Walk north, about six steps. A cutscene shows Giovanni's Nidoking and Rhydon wearing Palkia down while Ariana, Cyrus and Charon plan to stall you. Keep going north, about a dozen more steps: Cyrus and Charon team up for a **Double Battle** against you alone (the same two teams as above, 12 Pokémon in total).
4. Win and Giovanni's Beedrill finishes Palkia off. He catches it and leaves with the Lustrous Orb, holding all three "keys to the ultimate power". **Next:** report to the Pokémon League ([League HQ: the Trainer Affairs Department's investigations](07-league-to-cherrygrove.md#league-hq-the-trainer-affairs-departments-investigations-where-to-go-next)).
**Notes:**
- Losing either battle whites you out. Walk back in and the scene replays.

quests.title: Dialga, Palkia and Giratina: catch them (after Lance's visit)
evidence: **Who gets it / when:** after your final Hall of Fame entry and [Lance's visit to your house](01-pallet-to-pewter.md#pallet-town-lances-visit-home-after-the-final-hall-of-fame), the scene where he hands you the Team Rocket items. quests.title: Sinjoh Ruins (temple of Arceus): Regigigas and Arceus (after the final Hall of Fame)
evidence: **Warning: in a normal game you can't do this.** Both Pokémon need the **Azure Flute** after the story, and the Seven Island shrine keeper never gives it back: he only tells you to keep it safe ([Ritual Shrine: borrowing the Azure Flute](06-sevii-islands-indigo.md#ritual-shrine-borrowing-the-azure-flute-post-game-probably-unobtainable); [known issue](known-issues.md#arceus-and-regigigas-out-of-reach)). The flute is the only known way back into the temple after the story ([Ruins of Alph: small extras](08-cherrygrove-to-azalea.md#ruins-of-alph-small-extras)), and the only thing that makes the centre circle react. The steps below describe what the game data says would happen; they can't be confirmed in game.
**Who gets it / when:** after your final Hall of Fame entry, if you could get back in.

**How it would work:**
1. **Regigigas.** "Regigigas guards the temple. You must defeat it to climb the steps. Challenge Regigigas?" → Yes: wild **Regigigas, Lv. 95**. One chance: catching it, knocking it out or running away removes it, and the steps are open. Only a loss lets you retry (you white out).
2. **Arceus.** Step into the centre circle carrying the **Azure Flute** from the shrine keeper's post-game gift (a flute from anywhere else won't do), with **Dialga, Palkia and Giratina all in your party** ([previous entry](#dialga-palkia-and-giratina-catch-them-after-lances-visit)). "Use them to summon Arceus?" → Yes. The three appear and Arceus comes down. Talk to it: "Try to catch Arceus?" → Yes: wild **Arceus, Lv. 95**. One chance: catching it, knocking it out or running away removes it; only a loss lets you retry.

**Notes:**
- Palkia's space (the old Sinjoh Ruins) has a doorway at its north end that leads to the Mystri Stage, but you can't reach it, so it's no way in.
- The three circles around the stage belong to the original game's Arceus event ("Will you choose Dialga?"). In normal play they never react: they only work after a scene from that event, which needs a special event Arceus.

quests.title: Mt. Moon Square: the Clefairy dance (Monday nights)
evidence: **Who gets it / when:** every week, on **Monday from 8:00 p.m. to 11:59 p.m.** or **Tuesday from midnight to 3:59 a.m.**, by the DS clock.

**How it works:**
1. At that time, the doorway from the entrance into the Square takes you to a copy of the Square where six Clefairy dance around a rock. The game picks the doorway's destination when you enter the entrance cave, so if 8 p.m. passes while you're standing in it, go out and back in.
2. Walk in and head west, past the "Closed" sign. The scene plays when you reach the far west side of the area, about ten steps west and a few steps south of that sign.
3. When the dance ends, a **Moon Stone** appears where they danced, a few steps north-east of where you stand. Pick it up **before you leave**: if you go out and come back, the stone is gone and the doorway leads to the normal Square for the rest of that day.

**Notes:** once you've seen the dance, the doorway leads to the normal Square again until the day changes. The dance and a new Moon Stone come back **every Monday night**. Because the day changes at midnight, the dance can also play once more between midnight and 3:59 a.m. on Tuesday, even if you saw it on Monday evening (tested in an emulator: with the dance marked as seen at 10 p.m. on Monday the doorway leads to the normal Square, and once the clock passes midnight it leads to the dance again). The rest of the time the Square is the normal map with Asher's gang ([Pewter City to Vermilion City](02-pewter-to-vermilion.md)). This is the original game's event, kept by the hack.

quests.title: Ruins of Alph: the four stone panels and the chamber walls (continues Cherrygrove City to Azalea Town's Ruins of Alph entries)
evidence:
**How it works:**
1. **Panels:** examine the panel and rotate and slide the pieces until the picture is complete. When it's solved, the floor gives way and you drop into the **Underground Hall**. From then on, wild Unown appear in the Underground Hall. Nothing else is given.
2. **Walls:** examining a wall only shows a short line of Unown writing on a stone tablet. It gives no hint in words (tested in an emulator, all four chambers). Do what the table says and the wall crumbles. Tested in an emulator: the Escape Rope, Flash and the Water Stone each opened their wall when used while facing it, and you stay in the chamber (the Escape Rope doesn't take you out). A Water Stone used two steps back from the wall did nothing.
3. **Behind every wall** is the same place: the hall of the dream world from the Molly chapter ([Cherrygrove City to Azalea Town](08-cherrygrove-to-azalea.md)). This is the way back in for the post-game **Entei** rematch in [Cherrygrove City to Azalea Town](08-cherrygrove-to-azalea.md)'s "Ruins of Alph: small extras". Any of the four walls works, not just the Kabuto one. Whichever wall you came through, the hall's exit door at the bottom always leads back to the **Kabuto chamber**.
4. **Unown Report:** the researcher at the Research Center never writes any notes in your Unown Report. He only ever says that the ruins are "about 1,500 years old" (see [the known issue](known-issues.md#unown-report-notes)).

**Notes:** at the end of the Molly chapter the Kabuto wall closes again, so you have to reopen it. In the original game, each wall led to a small room with Unown writing. Those rooms are still in the game data, but nothing leads to them now. An earlier version of this guide said Island Forest on Six Island has no wild Pokémon until you've solved a panel; that's not so (see [the known issue](known-issues.md#island-forest-wild-pokémon)).

quests.title: Forest of Time: the maze of clearings (continues Ilex Forest and Goldenrod City's Forest of Time entries)
evidence: **Who gets it / when:** every time you go north through the forest: in the Sammy chapter ([Ilex Forest and Goldenrod City](09-ilex-goldenrod.md), "Sammy and the injured Celebi", step 5) and for the shrine (Shaymin, Celebi).

**Notes:**
- You arrive standing on an exit. Step off it before you choose the next one.
- The top-left and top-right exits take you only when you walk sideways into them (left or right). Walking up onto them does nothing.
- Wrong exits either loop you between clearings or drop you back at the entrance clearing.
- While the ranger has sent you for the medicine in the Sammy chapter, the last exit sends you back to the entrance clearing instead. The same happens from the moment Bugsy gives you the Honey for his bug hunt in Ilex Forest, and it goes on after the hunt until the old ranger in Ilex Forest starts the Sammy chapter. There's nothing for you at the shrine before that chapter anyway.
- During the Sammy chapter, Sammy, Celebi and the ranger stand on the entrance clearing's top-middle exit and block it until their scene moves on.
- On rc7 and earlier, don't enter the Forest of Time in the middle of Bugsy's bug hunt: the two share their progress, and the wrong scene may play. Fixed in rc8 (see [the known issue](known-issues.md#forest-of-time-during-the-bug-hunt)).
- Tested in an emulator: the route above leads to the upper forest once the Sammy chapter is over. During the medicine errand, and after the bug hunt has ended, the last exit puts you back at the bottom of the entrance clearing.

quests.title: Lake of Rage: when the "calm day" happens (continues Lake of Rage, Blackthorn City and beyond's lake trio and calm-day visitors)
evidence: **Who gets it / when:** on **Wednesdays**, once you've cleared the Team Rocket HQ in Mahogany Town (the scene where Green or Red goes home at the end of the HQ) **and** seen the Petrel scene at the lake guardian's house ([Lake of Rage, Blackthorn City and beyond](12-lake-of-rage-to-sinjoh.md)).

**How it works:**
1. The game checks when you **enter the Lake of Rage or Route 43** from another map. If it's Wednesday (by the DS clock) and the Rocket HQ is done, it marks the day as calm. On any other day it clears the mark.
2. On a calm day, once you've seen the Petrel scene, the lake shows Fisherman Carson (Red Scale), Wesley (the Wednesday sibling) and an item on the ground, and the lake trio's first encounter starts (Uxie, Mesprit and Azelf: see that entry in [Lake of Rage, Blackthorn City and beyond](12-lake-of-rage-to-sinjoh.md)). Before the Petrel scene none of them appear, even on a calm Wednesday.
3. The item on the ground is a **PP Max** if you pick it up between 7:00 p.m. and 6:59 a.m. by the DS clock, and a **Heart Scale** the rest of the day. It comes back on later calm Wednesdays, as long as you've visited the lake on a day other than Wednesday in between.

**Notes:** if you're already at the lake when the day changes, leave and come back so the check runs again. Prof. Hale's line that "the downpour over the Lake of Rage stops for one day every Wednesday" is accurate. Tested in an emulator: on a Wednesday after the Rocket HQ and the Petrel scene, Carson, Wesley, the item and the trio appear when you enter the lake. Before the Petrel scene, or on a Thursday, they don't. Entering Route 43 on a Wednesday also marks the day, entering on a Thursday clears the mark, and without the Rocket HQ no Wednesday is calm. The item's two time windows were not tested.
